<!-- name: Trailhead -->
<!-- board: Wardriving on the T-Watch S3 Plus | A dimmer status light | Bluetooth addresses the right way round -->
**Trailhead.** Squachy has spent his whole life indoors, listening to everything within fifty feet and never once knowing where he was. The T-Watch S3 Plus has a real GPS chip in it, so he's putting his boots on. He now logs every WiFi network and Bluetooth device he hears, and exactly where he heard it, then hands the whole lot over as a file WiGLE will take. Fair warning: this is the trailhead, not the summit. It works on the bench, with a pretend position. Nobody has walked it around the block yet. UK, you're up first. Tell us what breaks.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.25.0/docs/trailhead.gif" width="480" alt="Squachy on his main screen in the snow, then in the tunnel, then the STATUS LIGHT page with BRIGHTNESS at 1 of 7, then the Settings list with its headings as plain labels."></p>

**Wardriving, on the watch (new, not road-tested).** On a T-Watch S3 Plus, go to WATCH SETTINGS and tap WARDRIVE. The GPS wakes up, the row says GPS STARTING, then NO FIX YET while it hunts for satellites, then ON and a running count once it knows where it is. Give it a few minutes under open sky the first time, because a window sill won't cut it (we tried). From then on, every network and device gets written down with its position, and the same one near the same spot isn't written twice. It only writes while it has a fix, so nothing gets logged in the wrong place. The log lives on the watch, room for about 125,000 sightings, and it survives restarts and flat batteries.

**Getting it off the watch.** Plug the watch into a computer, open the web flasher in Chrome or Edge, and press DOWNLOAD WIGLE FILE. You get a WigleWifi-1.6 file, WiFi and Bluetooth together, ready for wigle.net/uploads. The log stays on the watch until you clear it, and a duress wipe takes it with everything else. Only the S3 Plus has a GPS: the row is there on the plain T-Watch S3 too, but it will sit at GPS STARTING forever, because there's nothing to start.

**A dimmer status light.** The lowest brightness on the status light was still bright enough to light a bedroom ceiling. BRIGHTNESS now has seven steps instead of five, and the two new ones sit underneath the old bottom. Step 1 is a faint glow you have to look for. Nobody's light changes on its own: whatever you had picked is still what you get.

**Bluetooth addresses the right way round.** Squachy has been printing Bluetooth addresses back to front, so nothing matched what your phone or any other scanner showed you. They're in the normal order now, everywhere he shows one. Thanks to the same eagle eye who caught the ghosts in Ghost Town.

**Settings stopped folding.** The headings in Settings used to fold their section away when tapped, which nobody asked for and nobody understood. They're plain labels now. Everything is just there.

**A new board, and a tidier board list.** The Sunton ESP32-2432S032C, the 3.2" IPS with the capacitive touch and the battery charger, has its own build on the web flasher. The flasher's board list was getting long, so it's grouped by family now, every entry shows the model code printed on the board, and there's a box where you type that code and it picks the right one for you. It has no way to read its battery, which is the board's doing, not Squachy's.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- Wardriving on the T-Watch S3 Plus (NEW, NOT ROAD-TESTED): WATCH SETTINGS > WARDRIVE switches the GPS and the log on together. WiFi networks (with their security, e.g. [WPA2-PSK-CCMP]) and Bluetooth devices (with their maker ID) are logged with position, altitude and accuracy, only while there's a fresh fix. The same device is logged again after 5 minutes or 50 metres.
- A 125,000-sighting log in the watch's spare flash, kept across restarts, cleared by a duress wipe.
- DOWNLOAD WIGLE FILE on the web flasher (desktop Chrome or Edge): a WigleWifi-1.6 CSV for wigle.net/uploads.
- A GPS counter on the watch's main screen while the GPS is on: satellites heard, and used.
- Console: GPS, GPS OFF, GPS STATUS, WARDRIVE ON/OFF, WIGLE, WIGLE CLEAR, and ADC (pin voltages, CYD boards).
- Sunton ESP32-2432S032C (3.2" IPS, GT911 capacitive touch) on the web flasher.
- The web flasher's board list is grouped by family, shows each board's model code, and has a code finder.

**Changed**
- Status light BRIGHTNESS has seven steps, not five; the two new ones are dimmer than the old lowest. Saved levels carry over unchanged.
- Settings headings are labels; they no longer fold their section away when tapped.
- The watch sets its clock from GPS time when it has a fix.

**Fixed**
- Bluetooth addresses were printed byte-reversed everywhere (LOG, detail pages, the console). They now match what other scanners show. (#22)
